title: Waiver and Upgrade Terms of the Travel Protection Plans
content:
Two terms of the Travel Protection Plans turn on the plan you hold rather than on anything you do later:
whether the plan can waive the exclusion of pre-existing medical conditions, and whether the cover may be
upgraded to a higher plan after it has been issued. Both carry their own window, counted in calendar days.

| Plan | Pre-existing condition waiver offered | Waiver purchase window (days) | Upgrade permitted after issue | Upgrade window (days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Trip Basics Essential | No | 0 | Yes | 14 |
| Trip Basics Standard | No | 0 | Yes | 14 |
| TripGuard Plus | Yes | 21 | Yes | 14 |
| TripGuard Premier | Yes | 21 | No | 0 |
| Cancel For Any Reason Elite | Yes | 14 | No | 0 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Traveller | Yes | 14 | Yes | 21 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Executive | Yes | 14 | No | 0 |

A window of 0 days is recorded against a plan that does not offer the term at all, and is not a window of no
length on a term that exists.

## The same terms put as conditions

Where your certificate is a Trip Basics Essential or a Trip Basics Standard, no waiver of pre-existing medical
conditions is available on it. Where it is a TripGuard Plus or a TripGuard Premier, the waiver is available and
the policy must have been bought within 21 days of the first payment toward the trip; on Cancel For Any Reason
Elite and on both Annual Multi-Trip plans the waiver is available on a window of 14 days.

Where your certificate is a TripGuard Premier, a Cancel For Any Reason Elite or an Annual Multi-Trip Executive,
it may not be upgraded to a higher plan once it has been issued. Where it is a Trip Basics Essential, a Trip
Basics Standard or a TripGuard Plus, an upgrade may be asked for within 14 days of issue; on Annual Multi-Trip
Traveller the same right runs for 21 days.
